title: Isolated installed wire schema validation versus unresolved native read latency
question: Does isolated native wire schema preparation itself account for the observed seconds-long completed demand reads?
method: Read-only exact-stage/OID/system check; authenticate the registered wire body against installed pg_proc; call the existing pg_jsonschema validator on tiny and installed read input/output schemas with a controlled null instance. No business data, demands, source or answers are read. Three diagnostic samples per schema, not a throughput or accuracy campaign.

outputs.role: Final diagnostic results on installed stage with JIT off

conclusion: The isolated installed read input/output schemas validate the controlled null instance in milliseconds on this stage; this does not support standalone schema preparation as the seconds-long latency source in this context. Full nonempty-page validation, nested native SQL and JIT causation remain unresolved. The temporary test host used default JIT on while the deployment policy disables it; profile alignment and actual matching-source retries remain required. This is not native consumer or provider qualification.
